Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 57, verses 4–7:

﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees what you do. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned. He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He is Knower of what is within the breasts.﴾

﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ He addresses the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿and spend from that of which He has made you successors (mustakhlafin) therein﴾, that is, making you possessors of it. That is: the wealth that was in the hands of others, so He destroyed them and gave it to Quraysh, and they became successors to those who had passed away in that wealth.

﴿So those among you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 57, verses 8–10:

﴿And what is wrong with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord, and He has taken your covenant?﴾ Abu 'Amr recited "ukhidha" (was taken) with a damma on the hamza and a kasra on the kha', and "mithaqukum" (your covenant) with a raf' on the qaf, in the passive form (ma lam yusamma fa'iluhu, the verb whose agent is not named). The others recited it with a fatha on the hamza, the kha' and the qaf, meaning: Allah took your covenant when He brought you forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, that Allah is your Lord and that you have no god besides Him. This was said by Mujahid.

It was also said: He took your covenant by establishing the proofs and the evidences that call to following the Messenger ﷺ, if you were believers at some point. So now is the most fitting time for you to believe, given the establishment of the proofs and the announcement of the mission of Muhammad ﷺ and the descent of the Qur'an.

﴿It is He who sends down to His servant﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿clear signs﴾ [meaning the Qur'an] ﴿that He may bring you out﴾ — Allah, through the Qur'an — ﴿from darknesses into light.﴾ It was also said: that the Messenger, through the call, may bring you out from darknesses into light, that is, from the darknesses of polytheism into the light of faith. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you.﴾

﴿And what is wrong with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, when to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth?﴾ He says: What excuse do you have for not spending on what brings you nearer to Allah, when you are mortal and will leave your wealth behind? Then He explained the virtue of those who preceded in spending in the way of Allah and in jihad, saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest.﴾ That is, the conquest of Makkah, according to the statement of most exegetes; al-Sha'bi said it was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. ﴿And fought﴾ — he says: those who spent their wealth and fought the enemy alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before the conquest of Makkah are not equal in virtue to those who spent and fought after it. ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterwards and fought.﴾

Muhammad ibn Fudayl reported from al-Kalbi that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (ra), for he was the first to embrace Islam and the first to spend his wealth in the way of Allah [see: al-Tabari: 27/220–221; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/219].

ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: The first to openly display his Islam with his sword was the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayyub informed us, Muhammad ibn Yunus informed us, al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAmr al-Shaybani informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari informed us, Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Adam ibn ʿAli, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and with him was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (ra), wearing a cloak which he had fastened at his chest with a toothpick. Then Jibril descended upon him and said: "Why do I see Abu Bakr wearing a cloak fastened at his chest with a toothpick?" So he (ﷺ) said: "He spent his wealth on me before the conquest." He said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Convey to him the greeting of peace and say to him: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours, or are you angry?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, conveys to you the greeting of peace and says to you: Are you pleased in this poverty of yours, or are you angry?" Abu Bakr said: "Shall I be angry with my Lord? I am pleased with my Lord, I am pleased with my Lord." [Cited by Ibn Kathir: 4/308 from al-Baghawi, and he said: "This hadith is weak in chain from this route, and Allah knows best." In its chain is al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAmr. Ibn Hibban said in al-Majruhin wa'l-Du'afa' (2/185): he narrates strange reports from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, and it is not permissible to argue with him at all, and he cited this hadith. al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan (3/103): abandoned (matruk), and he cited this hadith through the route of Ibn Khuzaymah, then said: "and it is a lie."]

﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾ — that is, to each of the two groups Allah promised Paradise. ʿAta' said: the degrees of Paradise vary, and those who spent before the conquest are in its best degrees. Ibn ʿAmir recited "wa-kullun" (each) with a raf'. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 57, verses 11–12:

﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him, and for him is a noble reward? On the Day when you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right.﴾ "Running before them" means upon the Sirat (the bridge over Hell). It is narrated that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari was sent to the reciters of the people of Basra, and three hundred men who had memorized the Qur'an entered upon him. He said to them: "You are the best and the reciters of the people of Basra. Recite it, and let the term not grow long upon you, lest your hearts harden as the hearts of those before you hardened."⁴

﴿And most of them are defiant﴾, meaning those who abandoned belief in 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ), peace be upon them both.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 57, verses 17–19:**

﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death. We have certainly made the signs clear to you, so that you may understand. Indeed, the male and female believers who give charity﴾. Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim, read "al-musaddiqin" and "al-musaddiqat" with a light *sad* (from *tasdiq*, "affirmation"), meaning the believing men and women. The others read them with a doubled *sad* (from *tasaddaq*, "giving charity"), meaning *al-mutasaddiqin* and *al-mutasaddiqat*, where the *ta'* is assimilated into the *sad* (*idgham*, "assimilation," the merging of one consonant into the next). ﴿And lend to Allah a good loan﴾, by giving charity and spending in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿It will be multiplied for them﴾, that loan, ﴿and they will have a noble reward﴾, a good recompense, which is Paradise.

﴿Those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the truthful (al-siddiqun)﴾. The *siddiq* (one who is greatly truthful, "the truthful") is the one who is very much given to truthfulness. Mujahid said: Everyone who believes in Allah and His Messenger is a *siddiq*, and he recited this verse.

Al-Dahhak said: They are eight men from this nation who preceded the people of the earth in their time to Islam: Abu Bakr, Ali, Zayd, Uthman, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, and Hamzah, and the ninth of them was Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them all. Allah joined him to them because of the truthfulness of his intention that He knew of.

﴿And the martyrs (al-shuhada') are with their Lord﴾. The scholars differed over the structure (*nazm*, "composition") of this verse. Some said: It is connected to what precedes it, and the *waw* is *waw al-nasaq* (the conjunctive *waw*, which links it to the previous phrase), and by "the martyrs" he meant the sincere believers. Al-Dahhak said: They are those whom we have named. Mujahid said: Every believer is a *siddiq* and a *shahid*, and he recited this verse.[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/276. See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/223.]]

Others said: The sentence is complete at His saying "they are the truthful," and then a new sentence begins: "and the martyrs are with their Lord," and the *waw* is *waw al-isti'naf* (the *waw* of resumption, which begins a new sentence). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Masruq, and a group. Then they differed about who these are. Some said: They are the prophets who bear witness over the nations on the Day of Resurrection. This is reported from Ibn Abbas,[[Mentioned by al-Tabari: 27/231.]] and it is the view of Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: They are those who were martyred in the way of Allah.[[See: al-Qurtubi: 17/253.]]

﴿For them is their reward﴾ for the righteous deeds they did, ﴿and their light﴾ on the Sirat (bridge), ﴿but those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim)﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 57, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted and mighty, ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs﴾ — with the signs and the proofs. ﴿And sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾ — meaning: justice. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: it is that by which things are weighed, i.e., "And We placed the Balance," as He said: "And the heaven He raised up, and He set the Balance" [al-Rahman: 7]. ﴿That mankind may maintain justice﴾ — so that they may deal with one another with justice.

﴿And We sent down iron﴾ — it is narrated from Ibn Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah sent down four blessings from the sky to the earth: iron, fire, water and salt." [[Weak. Narrated by al-Daylami in al-Firdaws. See Kanz al-Ummal: 15/418. Ibn Hajar attributed it in al-Kafi al-Shaf (p. 164) to al-Tha'labi and said: "In its chain is one whom I do not know."]] Ahl al-Ma'ani said that the meaning of His saying "We sent down iron" [i.e., We brought into being and created it; He brought forth iron for them from the ores] [[The text between the brackets is omitted in manuscript "A".]] and taught them its craft through His revelation.

Qutrub said: this is from the word nuzl (provision of hospitality), as one says: "The amir provided a good hospitality (anzala al-amir ala fulan nuzlan hasanan)," so the meaning of the verse is that He made it a provision for them. A similar usage is His saying: "And He sent down for you eight pairs of the cattle" [al-Zumar: 6].

﴿In it is mighty power﴾ — strong might, meaning weapons for war. Mujahid said: in it is protection (junnah) and weapons, meaning the instrument of defence and the instrument of striking. ﴿And benefits for mankind﴾ — things from which they benefit in their affairs, such as the knife, the axe, the needle and the like, since it is the tool of every craft. ﴿And that Allah may know﴾ — i.e., We sent Our messengers and sent down these things with them so that people might deal with truth and justice, and so that Allah may know and see ﴿who helps Him﴾ — i.e., His religion ﴿and His messengers unseen﴾ — i.e., he who stands in support of the religion while not having seen Allah or the Hereafter. Indeed, one who obeys Allah in the unseen is the one who is praised and rewarded. ﴿Indeed Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾ — Strong in His command, Mighty in His dominion.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 57, verse 26–27:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture. So among them is one who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient. Then We followed them up with Our messengers, and We followed up with Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they invented – We did not prescribe it for them – only seeking the pleasure of Allah. But they did not observe it with its proper observance.﴾ [[The words in brackets are missing from manuscript "A".]] ﴿Compassion﴾, which is the most tender softness; ﴿and mercy﴾, that they were fond of one another, just as Allah the Exalted said in describing the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "compassionate among themselves" [al-Fath: 29]. ﴿And monasticism, which they invented﴾ on their own initiative. This is not coordinated with what precedes it; its accusative case is governed by a hidden verb, as if he said: "And they invented monasticism," meaning they brought it on their own initiative. ﴿We did not prescribe it﴾, meaning We did not make it obligatory ﴿for them, except seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, meaning: rather, they sought the pleasure of Allah through that monasticism. That monasticism consisted of the hardships they imposed upon themselves through abstaining from food, drink, clothing, marriage, and worship in the mountains. ﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾, meaning they did not observe monasticism with its proper observance; rather they neglected it and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, so they became Jews and Christians, entered the religion of their kings, and abandoned asceticism. Some of them remained upon the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, until they encountered Muhammad ﷺ and believed in him. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So We gave those among them who believed their reward﴾, and they are those who persevered in it, and they are the people of compassion and mercy. ﴿And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, and they are those who abandoned monasticism and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him.

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Muzani informed us: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Shaiban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: al-Sa'q ibn Hazn narrated to us, from Aqil al-Ja'di, from Abu Ishaq, from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: "O Ibn Mas'ud, those before you divided into seventy-two sects, of which three were saved and the rest perished. One sect supported the kings and fought them for the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they seized them and killed them. And another group had no ability to confront the kings, nor to remain among them calling them to the religion of Allah and the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him; so they wandered through the lands and practised asceticism, and they are the ones about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And monasticism, which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them.'" Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in me, confirms me, and follows me, has observed it with its proper observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the ones who will perish."

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ on a donkey, and he said to me: "O son of Umm Abd, do you know from where the Children of Israel took up monasticism?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Tyrants prevailed over them after Jesus, peace be upon him, doing acts of disobedience. The people of faith became angry and fought them, but the people of faith were defeated three times, and only a few of them remained. They said: 'If these people prevail over us, they will wipe us out, and no one will remain to call to the religion.' So they said: 'Come, let us disperse throughout the earth until Allah sends the Prophet whom Jesus, peace be upon him, promised us,' meaning Muhammad ﷺ. So they dispersed into the caves of the mountains and innovated monasticism. Some of them held fast to their religion and some disbelieved." Then he recited this verse: "And monasticism, which they invented..." to the end of the verse. "So We gave those among them who believed..." meaning those who persevered in it, their reward. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "O son of Umm Abd, do you know what the monasticism of my community is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Migration and jihad, prayer and fasting, pilgrimage and the minor pilgrimage, and glorifying Allah on the hilltops."

It is also narrated from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Every nation has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this community is jihad in the way of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: After Jesus, peace be upon him, there were kings who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel and called them to the religion of Allah. It was said to their kings: "If you gathered these people who troubled you and killed them, or they would enter what we are in." Their kings gathered them and offered them death or leaving off reading the Torah and the Gospel, except for what they had altered from them. They said: "We will suffice you with ourselves." One group said: "Build for us a pillar, then raise us up to it, and give us something by which we can lift our food and drink, and we will not return to you." Another group said: "Let us wander in the earth and roam, and drink as the wild beasts drink; if you overcome us in a land, then kill us." Another group said: "Build for us dwellings in the wilderness, where we will dig wells and cultivate herbs, so we will not return to you nor pass by you." They did this to them. Those ones continued on the path of Jesus, peace be upon him, but there came after them a people who had altered the Book, and a man would say: "We will be in the place of so-and-so and worship as so-and-so worshipped, and wander as so-and-so wandered, and build dwellings as so-and-so built," while they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they imitated. This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "And monasticism, which they invented," that is, which those righteous ones invented. ﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾, meaning the later ones who came after them. ﴿So We gave those among them who believed their reward﴾, meaning those who invented it seeking the pleasure of Allah. "And many of them are defiantly disobedient," these are the ones who came after them. He said: When the Prophet ﷺ was sent and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his hermitage, a wanderer came from his wandering, and a monk from his monastery, and they believed in him.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾

He said: When the Prophet ﷺ was sent and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his hermitage, a wanderer came from his wandering, and a monk from his monastery, and they believed in him.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 57, verses 28–29:**

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾. The address is to the People of the Book, both the Jews and the Christians. He says: O you who have believed in Moses and Jesus, fear Allah regarding Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And believe in His Messenger﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿He will give you two portions﴾, meaning two shares, ﴿of His mercy﴾. That is, He will give you two rewards for your belief in Jesus (peace be upon him) and the Gospel, and for your belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an.

Some people said: the speech ends at His words "and mercy," and then a new statement begins: ﴿And monasticism, which they invented﴾. This is because they abandoned the truth, ate pork, drank wine, and abandoned ablution, ritual washing from major impurity, and circumcision. ﴿But they did not observe it with proper observance﴾, meaning the obedience and the religion, ﴿as it should have been observed﴾, a reference to something not mentioned. ﴿So We gave those who believed among them their reward﴾, and they are the people of compassion and mercy. ﴿But many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, and they are those who invented monasticism. Mujahid adopted this view.

The meaning of His words, ﴿except seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾: according to this interpretation, "We did not command them, nor did We prescribe for them, except seeking the pleasure of Allah, and We did not command them to practise asceticism" [this phrase is missing in manuscript "b"].

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ in Moses and Jesus, ﴿fear Allah﴾, and believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), "He will give you two portions of His mercy."

It has been related to us from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man who had a slave-girl, who taught her and taught her well, then freed her and married her; a man from the People of the Book who believed in his Book and believed in Muhammad (ﷺ); and a slave who worshipped Allah well and gave sincere counsel to his master." [Recorded by al-Bukhari in Knowledge, chapter on a man teaching his slave-girl and his family, 1/190; and Muslim in Faith, chapter on the obligation of believing in the message of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), no. 154, 1/134–135; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/53.]

﴿And He will make for you a light by which you will walk﴾. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: this means on the Sirat (the bridge over Hellfire). This is like His words: "Their light will run before them" (al-Tahrim: 8). It is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the light is the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it is guidance and clarity, meaning He will make for you a clear path in the religion by which you will be guided. ﴿And He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

It was said: when those among the People of the Book who had not believed heard His words, Mighty and Majestic: "Those will be given their reward twice" (al-Qasas: 54), they said to the Muslims: "As for those of us who believe in your Book, they will have their reward twice, for believing in your Book and in our Book. But as for those of us who do not believe, they will have a reward like yours. So what is your superiority over us?" Then Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two portions of His mercy﴾. So He made for them two rewards when they believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and He added to them light and forgiveness. [Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/66–68, to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id, 7/121: "Al-Tabarani related it, and in its chain is someone I do not know."] Then He said: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾, ﴿so that the People of the Book may know﴾. Qatada said: those among the People of the Book who did not believe envied the believers among them, so Allah, Exalted, revealed: "So that the People of the Book may know." [Recorded by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Tafsir, 2/276, and al-Tabari, 27/246. Al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/68, added that he attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]

Mujahid said: the Jews said, "A Prophet is about to emerge from among us who will cut off hands and feet." When he emerged from the Arabs, they disbelieved in him, so Allah, Exalted, revealed: "So that the People of the Book may know." That is, so that they may know, and "la" (not) is an extraneous particle. ﴿That they have no power over anything of Allah's bounty﴾, that is, so that those who did not believe may know that they have no reward and no share in Allah's bounty. ﴿And that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾ [Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/68, to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Your term, in comparison to the terms of the nations that passed, is like the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset.
